docs.title: aiowapy
docs.text:
An asynchronous WhatsApp Multi-Device client for Python. The protocol is implemented from scratch — Noise handshake, Signal (X3DH + double ratchet), WABinary codec, sender keys, media encryption, app state — with cryptography as the only crypto dependency.

No official Cloud API, no Go bridge, no subprocess: import aiowapy and go.

Unofficial client

Using this library violates WhatsApp's Terms of Service and the number may be banned. Use a test number and proceed at your own risk.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
pip install aiowapy

The distribution is called aiowapy, the import is wapy:

from aiowapy import Client

Real output of examples/offline_demo.py. The server is scripted; the Signal sessions, stanzas and the session file are the production code.

docs.title: A bot in 20 lines
docs.text:
import asyncio

from aiowapy import Client
from aiowapy.events import MessageEvent
from aiowapy.router import F


async def main() -> None:
    async with Client("bot.session") as client:
        print("connected as", client.info.jid)

        @client.router.message(F.text.startswith("/ping"))
        async def ping(event: MessageEvent) -> None:
            await client.send_text(event.chat_jid, "pong", quote=event.message_id)

        await client.run()


asyncio.run(main())

The first run prints a QR code (or use a pairing code — see Quick start). After that the session file keeps the keys and later runs only log in.

docs.title: What you get
docs.text:
Area Highlights Connection Noise XX handshake, WABinary frames, keepalive, automatic reconnect Pairing QR code and phone-number pairing, prekey publication 1:1 chat text, replies, reactions, edits, revokes, receipts (delivery/read) Media images, video, audio, voice notes, documents, stickers — upload and download Groups info, create, add/remove/promote/demote, leave, sender keys Reception prekey and one-time prekey sessions, sender keys, retry receipts Presence available/unavailable, subscriptions, typing indicators Storage one .session SQLite file with chats, contacts, messages, reactions History history sync chunks from the phone, stored and queryable App state patch sync with integrity hash, mute/pin/mark-read/push-name

Not implemented: calls, channels (newsletters), statuses, polls and buttons, LID-based encryption. See Protocol and limitations.

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:
• Quick start — link a device and send the first message.
  • Sending — text, replies, reactions, edits, revokes.
  • Receiving — events, router, filters.
  • Storage and history — what lives in .session and how to query it.
  • API reference — every public class and method.

docs.title: App state
docs.text: Contacts, mutes, pins, archives and read markers are not messages: they live in a key-value store synchronized through patches. The phone owns the keys and shares them with linked devices; patches are encrypted with those keys, chained by an additive integrity hash.

docs.title: Sync
docs.text:
results = await client.sync_app_state()
for result in results:
    print(result.name, result.version, result.applied, result.skipped)

Each collection (critical_block, critical_unblock_low, regular, regular_high, regular_low) is fetched from the stored version, verified and applied. Unknown mutations are counted as skipped instead of failing the whole patch.

What is verified:

Check Detail Value MAC HMAC-SHA512 over operation, key id and ciphertext, truncated Index MAC HMAC-SHA256 of the JSON index Patch MAC snapshot MAC, value MACs, version and collection name Integrity LTHash: 128-byte additive hash over WhatsApp Patch Integrity

Local copy:

entries = await client.app_state_entries("regular_high")
for index_json, value, timestamp in entries:
    print(index_json, timestamp)

docs.title: Writing
docs.text:
await client.mute_chat(jid, True)          # mute forever
await client.pin_chat(jid, True)
await client.mark_chat_read(jid, True)
await client.set_push_name("bot")

Each call builds one patch, updates the integrity hash and pushes it. The reply is checked for a type="error" collection; a conflict raises AppStateSyncError.

docs.title: Keys
docs.text:
Keys arrive from the phone in a protocol message (AppStateSyncKeyShare). The library stores them, then runs a sync in the background:

@client.router.on(NotificationEvent)
async def notifications(event: NotificationEvent) -> None:
    print(event.kind)

If a key is missing when a patch arrives, syncing that collection fails with AppStateSyncError; the local copy stays untouched.

docs.title: Groups
docs.text: Group messages do not use per-device Signal sessions for the body. The sender creates a sender key — a symmetric chain shared by the group members — encrypts once and signs the ciphertext. The key distribution message (SKDM) travels pairwise to every member device, attached to the same stanza.

docs.title: Sending
docs.text:
await client.send_text("120363000000000001@g.us", "hello everyone")
await client.send_image(group_jid, data, caption="look")

Nothing special is needed: send_text/send_media detect @g.us and switch to the group pipeline. Under the hood one stanza contains:

  • <participants> with one <enc type="pkmsg"> per member device (the SKDM),
  • a single <enc type="skmsg"> with the encrypted body,
  • a phash attribute summarizing the participant list.

docs.title: Querying
docs.text:
info = await client.group_info(group_jid)
print(info.subject, info.owner_jid, info.is_locked, info.disappearing_timer)
for participant in info.participants:
    print(participant.jid, participant.is_admin, participant.is_super_admin)

groups = await client.joined_groups()

Results are cached for 5 minutes in the session file; group_info(jid, refresh=True) forces a server round trip.

docs.title: Managing
docs.text:
group = await client.create_group("Team", [jid1, jid2])

await client.update_group_participants(group, "add", [jid3])
await client.update_group_participants(group, "remove", [jid3])
await client.update_group_participants(group, "promote", [jid4])
await client.update_group_participants(group, "demote", [jid4])

await client.leave_group(group)

Participant JIDs are stripped of their device suffix before they are sent: group membership is per user, not per device.

docs.title: Receiving
docs.text:
A group message arrives with from set to the group and participant set to the sender. The library:

  1. decrypts the pairwise <enc> entries, which carry the sender key distribution,
  2. stores the sender key under (group, sender),
  3. decrypts the <enc type="skmsg"> payload,
  4. dispatches MessageEvent with chat_jid = group and sender_jid = participant.

Out-of-order delivery is handled: skipped iterations are cached and replayed, up to 2000 messages ahead. A message older than the chain is rejected.

docs.title: Not implemented
docs.text:
• joining by invite link (chat.whatsapp.com/...),
  • invite link creation and revocation,
  • community/sub-group operations,
  • privacy tokens for adding contacts you have never talked to.

docs.title: Media
docs.text: Attachments are encrypted locally, uploaded to a WhatsApp media host and only the metadata travels through the chat socket.

docs.title: Sending
docs.text:
await client.send_image(chat, picture_bytes, caption="look")
await client.send_video(chat, video_bytes, caption="clip", seconds=12)
await client.send_audio(chat, ogg_bytes, voice_note=True, seconds=8)
await client.send_document(
    chat, pdf_bytes, file_name="report.pdf", mime_type="application/pdf"
)

Or the generic form:

from aiowapy.protocol.media import MEDIA_IMAGE

await client.send_media(
    chat,
    data,
    MEDIA_IMAGE,
    caption="text",
    mime_type="image/jpeg",
    width=1280,
    height=720,
)

What happens under the hood:

  1. A random 32-byte media key is generated.
  2. The file is encrypted with AES-256-CBC and an HMAC-SHA256 truncated to 10 bytes; the key is expanded with HKDF using WhatsApp Image Keys (or Video/Audio/Document).
  3. file_sha256 and file_enc_sha256 are computed.
  4. The encrypted blob is POSTed to a media host obtained from <iq xmlns="w:m">.
  5. The message contains url, direct path, media key, hashes and size.

docs.title: Receiving
docs.text:
Incoming attachments arrive as metadata in the MessageEvent; the bytes are downloaded on demand:

@client.router.message(F.media("image"))
async def on_image(event: MessageEvent) -> None:
    data = await client.download_media(event.media)

download_media fetches the encrypted blob, verifies its MAC, decrypts it and checks file_sha256 against the metadata. A mismatch is an error, not silent corruption.

Messages read back from the session file work the same way:

for message in await client.get_chat_history(chat, limit=20):
    if message.media:
        data = await client.download_stored(message)

docs.title: Types and field mapping
docs.text:
Media type Message field HKDF info image ImageMessage WhatsApp Image Keys video VideoMessage WhatsApp Video Keys audio / ptt AudioMessage WhatsApp Audio Keys document DocumentMessage WhatsApp Document Keys sticker StickerMessage WhatsApp Image Keys

Captions, file names, durations (seconds), dimensions and the voice-note flag are carried in the same protobuf and round-trip through the session file.

docs.title: Thumbnails and streaming
docs.text: JPEG thumbnails, video sidecars and streaming metadata are not produced. Clients show a placeholder instead of a preview until the file is downloaded.

docs.title: Sending
docs.text: Every send goes through Messenger: it enumerates the recipient's devices, encrypts one Signal message per device, wraps everything into a <message> stanza and waits for the server ack.

docs.title: Text
docs.text:
result = await client.send_text("49123456789@s.whatsapp.net", "hello")
print(result.message_id, result.sent, result.failed, result.acked)

SendResult has four fields:

Field Meaning message_id id of the stanza, also stored in the session file sent device JIDs the payload was encrypted for failed (device_jid, reason) for devices that could not be encrypted acked True/False for the server ack, None if not awaited

A message counts as delivered when at least one device accepted it; per-device failures are reported, not raised. wait_for_message=False returns immediately after the frame is on the wire.

docs.title: Replies
docs.text:
await client.send_text(chat, "answer", quote=message_id)

The quoted message is looked up in the session file, so its text, sender and id are attached as ContextInfo. A reply to a message the bot never saw still works, just without the quoted body.

docs.title: Reactions
docs.text:
await client.send_reaction(chat, message_id, "\U0001f44d")
await client.send_reaction(chat, message_id, "")      # retract

Incoming reactions are stored per sender and dispatched as ReactionEvent; read them with await client.reactions(chat, message_id).

docs.title: Edit and delete
docs.text:
await client.edit_message(chat, message_id, "corrected text")
await client.revoke_message(chat, message_id)

Incoming edits update the stored row, incoming revokes blank its text and mark it delete. Both produce EditEvent and RevokeEvent.

docs.title: Message types in the stanza
docs.text: The type attribute of <message> is set per content: text, reaction, image, video, audio, ptt, document, sticker. Group messages add a single <enc type="skmsg"> next to the per-device <participants> block.

docs.title: Send results are stored
docs.text: Every outgoing message is written to .session with outgoing=True, so history returns the conversation as a whole. Media descriptions are stored too, which is what download_stored() uses.

docs.title: Presence
docs.text:
await client.send_presence(True)            # available, announces the push name
await client.send_presence(False)           # unavailable

await client.subscribe_presence(jid)        # ask for this user's updates

await client.send_typing(jid, composing=True)
await client.send_typing(jid, composing=True, media="audio")   # recording a voice note
await client.send_typing(jid, composing=False)                 # stopped

Incoming updates arrive as events:

@client.router.on(PresenceEvent)
async def presence(event: PresenceEvent) -> None:
    if event.available:
        print(event.jid, "is online")
    elif event.last_seen:
        print(event.jid, "last seen", event.last_seen)
    # last_seen is None when the user hides it (last="deny")

@client.router.on(ChatStateEvent)
async def typing(event: ChatStateEvent) -> None:
    print(event.jid, event.state, event.media)

Notes:

  • The bot is announced as available right after connecting; without it contacts see no name.
  • The server only forwards presence for users you subscribed to, and usually only while you are online yourself.
  • last with the value deny means the user hides their last-seen time; the library maps it to last_seen=None.

docs.title: How it fits together
docs.text:
Client            public API: connect, send, receive, reconnect
├── Router / events       application handlers and filters
├── Messenger             device list -> Signal ciphertext -> <message> stanza
│   ├── DeviceResolver    usync + prekey bundles, cached
│   ├── SignalSessions    X3DH + double ratchet, stored per device
│   └── NodeSender        transport send + ack correlation
├── MessageReceiver       decrypt pairwise and sender-key payloads
├── GroupService          group info and membership
├── GroupSender           sender keys (SKDM + skmsg)
├── MediaStorage          media upload/download, CDN metadata
├── AppStateSync          patches, MACs, LTHash
├── HistorySyncService    encrypted history blobs
└── SessionStore          one SQLite file
NodeStream -> WhatsAppTransport -> Noise -> WebSocket

Layer rules are enforced by a test: protocol and crypto never import the client, store never imports the network, and so on.

docs.title: Wire details worth knowing
docs.text:
• Frames are [3-byte length][body]; the first frame is prefixed with the WA intro header.
  • Noise is XX with the WhatsApp prologue; the transport keys are derived per direction.
  • Server errors during pairing arrive as stream:error with the code in an attribute, not a child node. 515 means "device accepted, reconnect with a login payload".
  • <message> carries per-device payloads inside <participants>; a group body is a single <enc type="skmsg"> at the root.
  • Prekey messages include a <device-identity> blob so the receiver can check which device started the session.
  • Server iq type="set" requests must be answered with an iq type="result" carrying the same id, otherwise the connection is dropped.

docs.title: Status
docs.text:
The implementation is covered by 700+ offline tests, including cross-checks where one side of a Signal or sender-key session is built by test code and decrypted by the library.

Live traffic has not been exercised yet. The account used for development is rate-limited by WhatsApp on device linking, so no message has been delivered end to end in production. Treat the first live run as validation, not as a formality.

docs.title: Not implemented
docs.text: Missing Impact Calls none for bots Channels (newsletters) cannot read or post to channels Statuses cannot view or post stories Polls, buttons, lists no structured messages LID-based encryption sessions start on phone-number devices; LID mappings are stored but unused Privacy tokens (tctoken) adding strangers to groups may be rejected Group invite links cannot join or create invite links History on demand history arrives only when the phone sends it Thumbnails, streaming sidecars no previews for media

docs.title: Reference implementations
docs.text: Behaviour was cross-checked against whatsmeow (MPL-2.0) and Baileys (MIT). No code is copied: the wire formats and state machines were re-implemented, and this project stays MIT.

docs.title: 1. Link the device
docs.text: A companion device has to be linked once. Two ways, both in aiowapy.session.

docs.title: QR code
docs.text:
import asyncio

from aiowapy import Client


def show_qr(item: object) -> None:
    # item.qr holds the string WhatsApp expects; item.ascii is the terminal rendering
    print(item.ascii)  # type: ignore[attr-defined]


async def main() -> None:
    client = Client("bot.session", qr_callback=show_qr)
    await client.connect()
    print("ready:", client.info.jid)
    await client.run()


asyncio.run(main())

Open WhatsApp → Linked devices → Link a device and scan. The callback is called again with a fresh code when the current one expires.

docs.title: Pairing code
docs.text:
Typing a code on the phone is the alternative when a camera is not available:

from aiowapy.protocol.pairing_code import generate_pairing_code
from aiowapy.protocol.transport import WhatsAppTransport
from aiowapy.session import ClientSession

code = generate_pairing_code()
print("type this on the phone:", code)

session = ClientSession(
    "bot.session",
    transport_factory=lambda: WhatsAppTransport(),
)
state = await session.pair_with_phone_number("+49123456789", code)

A complete runnable version with node logging: examples/pair_code.py.

Both flows write the credentials into the session file, so the next start logs in directly.

docs.title: 2. Connect
docs.text:
client = Client("bot.session")
info = await client.connect()      # returns ClientInfo(jid, lid, push_name)
...
await client.close()

connect() returns when the server accepts the login. Serving continues in the background until close(). If you want to block, use await client.run().

docs.title: 3. Send something
docs.text:
await client.send_text("49123456789@s.whatsapp.net", "hello")

The recipient JID is the phone number followed by @s.whatsapp.net; groups end with @g.us.

docs.title: 4. Handle messages
docs.text:
from aiowapy.events import MessageEvent
from aiowapy.router import F


@client.router.message(F.text)
async def echo(event: MessageEvent) -> None:
    await client.send_text(event.chat_jid, event.text or "")

docs.title: Lifecycle notes
docs.text:
• Reconnect is automatic: dropped sockets and stream:error 515 are retried with exponential backoff. A 401/403/409 while connected stops the client — the device was revoked and re-pairing is a user decision.
  • Keepalive is a node-level <iq xmlns="w:p"><ping/></iq> every 30 seconds; the connection counts as dead after 35 seconds of silence.
  • Session file is created with 0600 permissions. It contains the private keys: treat it like a password.

docs.title: Receiving
docs.text: Incoming stanzas are decrypted, turned into events and handed to the router. Handlers can be sync or async; a failing handler is logged and does not stop the others.

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
from aiowapy.events import (
    ChatStateEvent,
    ConnectedEvent,
    DisconnectedEvent,
    EditEvent,
    HistorySyncEvent,
    MessageEvent,
    NotificationEvent,
    PresenceEvent,
    ReactionEvent,
    ReceiptEvent,
    RevokeEvent,
)

@client.router.on(ReceiptEvent)
async def on_receipt(event: ReceiptEvent) -> None:
    print(event.receipt_type, event.message_ids)
Event When MessageEvent decrypted text/attachment, live or from history sync ReactionEvent emoji reaction, text empty when retracted EditEvent someone edited a message RevokeEvent someone deleted a message for everyone HistorySyncEvent a history chunk was stored ReceiptEvent delivery/read confirmation PresenceEvent user came online/offline, last seen ChatStateEvent typing/recording indicator ConnectedEvent / DisconnectedEvent connection lifecycle NotificationEvent server notifications not modeled yet (device changes, ...)

docs.title: Filters
docs.text:
aiowapy.router.F builds small predicates; combine them with &, |, ~:

from aiowapy.router import F

@client.router.message(F.text.startswith("/start"))
async def start(event: MessageEvent) -> None: ...

@client.router.message(F.text.contains("invoice") & F.chat("1203630@g.us"))
async def invoice(event: MessageEvent) -> None: ...

@client.router.message(~F.from_me() & F.media("image"))
async def photo(event: MessageEvent) -> None: ...

@client.router.message(F.custom(lambda e: len(e.text or "") > 500))
async def long_text(event: MessageEvent) -> None: ...

Available: F.text (.contains, .startswith, .endswith, .equals), F.chat, F.sender, F.message_id, F.from_me, F.media(type), F.custom(predicate).

docs.title: Reading a message
docs.text:
@client.router.message(F.text)
async def handler(event: MessageEvent) -> None:
    print(event.chat_jid)      # where it came from
    print(event.sender_jid)    # who wrote it (group participant for groups)
    print(event.message_id)
    print(event.text)
    print(event.timestamp)     # unix seconds from the server
    print(event.media)         # MediaInfo or None
    print(event.from_me)
    print(event.raw)           # the original Node, if you need more

docs.title: Read and delivery receipts
docs.text:
Incoming messages are acknowledged automatically (receipt type="delivery"), which is what makes your bot look online. Turn it off with auto_receipts=False and send your own:

await client.mark_read(event)                # receipt type="read"
await client.mark_read(event, receipt_type="delivery")

docs.title: Retry receipts
docs.text:
If decryption fails, the library asks the sender to resend (receipt type="retry"), and from the second attempt it includes a fresh one-time prekey so the sender can start a new session. Five attempts is the ceiling.

If our outgoing message fails on the other side, they send us a retry request; the library drops the broken session and resends the stored payload from its outbox.

docs.title: Handler errors
docs.text: router.on_error receives (exception, event); without it the traceback is logged. One broken handler never silences the rest.

docs.title: Storage and history
docs.text: *.session is a single SQLite file that holds the whole state of the account, in the spirit of Pyrogram: credentials, Signal sessions, prekeys, app state, chats, contacts, messages and reactions.

docs.title: Chats and contacts
docs.text:
chats = await client.get_chats()          # newest conversation first
users = await client.get_users()          # contacts the bot has seen
groups = await client.get_groups()

chat = await client.get_chat(jid)
print(chat.name)          # contact name -> push name -> subject -> jid
print(chat.kind)          # "user" or "group"
print(chat.last_message_at, chat.total_messages)

Names are refined, never wiped: a None from a later stanza does not erase what is already stored. A push name comes from the notify attribute of incoming messages and from history sync; a contact name is yours:

await client.set_contact_name(jid, "Mom")
await client.save_contact(jid, "Mom", phone="49123456789")

docs.title: Message history
docs.text:
history = await client.get_chat_history(chat_jid, limit=50)
for message in history:                   # newest first
    print(message.timestamp, message.sender_jid, message.text, message.outgoing)

older = await client.get_chat_history(
    chat_jid, limit=50, before_timestamp=history[-1].timestamp
)

one = await client.get_message(chat_jid, message_id)

A stored message carries the full attachment description, so downloading works months later:

data = await client.download_stored(message)

You can write rows yourself — useful for importing an export or seeding a bot:

await client.save_message(chat_jid, message_id, "hello", sender_jid=jid, timestamp=now)

docs.title: Reactions
docs.text: pairs = await client.reactions(chat_jid, message_id)   # [(sender_jid, emoji), ...]

docs.title: History sync
docs.text:
WhatsApp sends history to a new device in encrypted chunks announced by a protocol message. The library downloads, decrypts and unpacks them, writes peers and messages to the session file, and emits HistorySyncEvent:

@client.router.on(HistorySyncEvent)
async def on_chunk(event: HistorySyncEvent) -> None:
    print(f"{event.chats} chats, {event.messages} messages, more={event.has_more}")

The chunk format:

Step Detail Announcement ProtocolMessage type 5 with HistorySyncNotification Payload encrypted blob on a media host, media type md-msg-hist Encoding AES-CBC + HMAC, then gzip, then protobuf HistorySync Content conversations, messages, push names, phone→LID mappings

Duplicates are filtered: a message id is stored once, no matter how many chunks mention it.

docs.title: Tables
docs.text:
Table Contents creds device credentials (private keys, base64) prekeys one-time prekeys and their upload state sessions Signal session records per device JID sender_keys sender key chains per (group, member) peers users and groups with names messages messages, outgoing flag, media JSON reactions one row per (chat, message, sender) deleted_messages revoked message ids lid_mappings phone-number JID → LID JID app_state_* sync keys, collection versions and the local copy groups cached group metadata

Migrations are numbered files in wapy/store/migrations/; the schema version lives in meta.

docs.title: Client
docs.text:
Client(
    path: Path | str,
    *,
    transport_factory: Callable[[], Transport]
    | None = None,
    qr_callback: Callable[[object], Awaitable[None] | None]
    | None = None,
    push_name: str = DEFAULT_PUSH_NAME,
    platform: str = "chrome",
    version: tuple[int, int, int] = DEFAULT_VERSION,
    ack_timeout: float = DEFAULT_ACK_TIMEOUT,
    auto_receipts: bool = True,
    media_transport: MediaTransport | None = None,
    node_observer: Callable[[Node], None] | None = None,
    sent_observer: Callable[[Node], None] | None = None,
    reconnect: bool = True,
    reconnect_delay: float = 1.0,
    max_reconnect_delay: float = MAX_RECONNECT_DELAY,
)

A connected WhatsApp session.

Usage:

client = Client("bot.session", qr_callback=show_qr)
await client.connect()
await client.send_text("4917...@s.whatsapp.net", "hi")
await client.run()          # serves until closed

docs.title: connect async
docs.text:
connect() -> ClientInfo

Log in (pairing first if the session file is new) and start serving.

Returns as soon as the server accepts the login payload. Pairing through a QR code calls qr_callback from the connection task while this method waits.

docs.title: run async
docs.text:
run() -> None

Connect and then serve until close() is called.

docs.title: close async
docs.text:
close() -> None

Stop serving and release the session file.

docs.title: sync_app_state async
docs.text:
sync_app_state() -> list[SyncedCollection]

Pull app state patches (contacts, mutes, pins, ...) for every collection.

Requires sync keys, which WhatsApp shares from the phone; without them the call raises and the local copy stays as it is.

docs.text:
save_message(
    chat_jid: str,
    message_id: str,
